articles.headline: Week 2 impact on the NFC: Caleb Williams, Jayden Daniels hurt
articles.description: Caleb Williams and Jayden Daniels both got injured. The Packers nearly lost to the Jets. The Saints upset the Ravens. And three teams have a claim as the NFC's best.
articles.body:
It's hard to say that any week of an NFL season can feel seismic, especially when it's the second week of the campaign. But I believe we're going to look back on Week 2 and say it was extraordinarily impactful in deciding and decoding the NFC.

Injuries to young quarterbacks were the biggest stories of the day, but we also saw several of the conference's top contenders reaffirm themselves with big victories, a couple of teams we're still not sure about squeak by and a preseason contender narrowly save itself from the 0-2 cliff. We even saw the NFC South get on the board with a pair of victories.

Subscribe: 'The Bill Barnwell Show'

Let's run through some of the results and events from Sunday that might really matter in the NFC's big picture and break down how they played out and how they impact the conference moving forward. I'll start in Dallas, where the Commanders are facing serious short- and long-term questions about what's next.

Jump to:

WSH and Daniels' injury

CHI and Williams' injury

NO and its big win

GB and its near loss

Three teams at the top

Washington Commanders (0-2)

Lost 37-20 to the Cowboys

Sunday showed why organizations were both transfixed and terrified by the idea of drafting Jayden Daniels as their quarterback of the future. For most of the first half, Daniels was singlehandedly propelling the Commanders forward on offense. In addition to going 11-of-17 for 96 yards as a passer, he picked up five first downs with his legs, scrambling seven times for 69 yards. Having a QB capable of bailing the offense out and picking up explosive plays in the process gives the Commanders a floor that most other teams don't have on a weekly basis.

And then, on the final play of the first half, we saw the other side of the coin. With the Commanders passing up a field goal attempt to try to score a touchdown with three seconds remaining, Daniels took the snap from under center and got caught up in the footwork of left guard Chris Paul. As Daniels fell to the ground, he tried to brace with his left elbow, only for it to visibly give way and dislocate. He somehow got up and threw an incomplete pass and then did not return after halftime in a game that got away from Washington after the break.

The injury is likely to sideline Daniels for an extended period. He missed four games after dislocating the same elbow in Week 9 a year ago, then reaggravated the injury in Week 14 and did not return over the remainder of the season. Missing a month would be a season-altering injury for the Commanders, who are already 0-2 and about to face the defending champion Seahawks in their home opener next week. Marcus Mariota is a capable backup, but the veteran doesn't offer the same sort of explosiveness and calmness under pressure that Daniels exhibited during his remarkable rookie season.

articles.headline: 2026 MLB awards tracker: Odds for MVP, Cy Young, Rookie of the Year
articles.description: Who are the favorites to win seasonlong honors? Here are the odds for MVP, Cy Young and Rookie of the Year in the AL and NL.
articles.body:
As the season winds down its final week of play, Pete Crow-Armstrong is running away with the National League MVP award, to the point where no action is being taken any longer, with Shohei Ohtani on the IL. Yordan Alvarez has also seemingly locked up the American League MVP honor with -6000 odds, with Junior Caminero the only close challenger at 13-1.

The AL Cy Young race is also all but done from a betting perspective, with no lines being currently listed. Cam Schlittler seems to be a near-lock to claim the trophy, with only Dylan Cease in the ever-quieting conversation. On the NL side, Jacob Misiorowski looks to be well on his way to winning his first Cy Young award, showing -8000 odds to Chris Sale's 20-1.

Meanwhile, the NL Rookie of the Year race is also no longer showing lines, with RBI-machine Sal Stewart as the clear top choice. In the AL, Kevin McGonigle is the solid favorite at -3500, with Parker Messick coming in at a distant 13-1.

articles.headline: Antoine Semenyo happy to lead Man City's attack if needed
articles.description: Antoine Semenyo is ready to take on the challenge of leading Manchester City's attack if needed.
articles.body:
Antoine Semenyo is ready to take on the challenge of leading Manchester City's attack if needed.

The Ghana international underlined his finishing ability with two clinical strikes in City's thrilling 5-3 victory over Sunderland in the Premier League on Sunday.

The prolific output of Erling Haaland, who was also on target as Enzo Maresca's side maintained their 100% start to the campaign, means City are rarely short of goals.

But the club's summer transfer activity has left them with no clear replacement for Haaland should the Norwegian miss any games.

Maresca has identified winger Semenyo as the most obvious alternative and the 26-year-old would be happy to step up.

Semenyo said: "I've heard about his backup striker thing. I don't know where it's come from!

"But, yes, if I need to, then I'll do it. I've no problem in doing that."

Of his finishing, he added: "I think that just comes naturally.

"Once I'm in front of the goal, I know it doesn't move. So as long as I hit it in the corner, hit it with a good connection, I know it will go in."

City were pushed all the way by Sunderland, who showed no sign of weariness from their midweek Europa League outing.

Brian Brobbey scored a hat trick for the visitors but Semenyo's double and Haaland's late effort completed the job for City, for whom Enzo Fernández and Rayan Cherki also struck.

Both sides had numerous other chances in a frantic game. Haaland missed an open goal for City while Brobbey hit the bar and Rúben Dias had to clear off the line. Sunderland also felt they should have had a penalty for handball against Elliot Anderson.

Semenyo said: "It was a tough one. Physically, we knew it would be like that -- duels, aerial balls, set-pieces.

"We knew it would be a fight, and we just needed to stick together collectively and win our individual duels and get three points, which we've done.

"Sometimes it is going to be like that, not every game you can control. You just have to ride the waves. We knew if we got our chances, we would score."

- Erling Haaland sets unique goal milestone as Man City beat Sunderland

- Enzo Maresca relieved as Manchester City pass difficult Sunderland test

City have now won seven games in succession in all competitions since their defeat by Arsenal in the Community Shield.

With a three-point lead at the top of the Premier League, it has been a strong start under new manager Maresca but Semenyo feels there is still room for improvement yet.

He said: "Everyone feels good. It's where we want to be, but we're not going to get too complacent, too relaxed. We know that there's a lot more games to go.

"We just want to continue winning, we just have to keep going.

"It's seven or eight weeks we've been together now, so it's not been too long, but we're doing well. We're winning our games and we'll keep improving."

articles.headline: Every team's odds to win the World Series: Dodgers remain favorites as playoffs loom
articles.description: Every MLB team's odds to win the 2026 World Series, led by the Dodgers. Milwaukee and Tampa Bay continue to see odds improvement.
articles.body:
After multiple months of having the best record in Major League Baseball, the Milwaukee Brewers remain the second-favorite to win the 2026 World Series, shortening to +600 from +650 week-over-week. The New York Yankees, previously in that slot are tied for third-best with the AL-leading Tampa Bay Rays at +850.

The Los Angeles Dodgers are still the World Series favorites -- as they have been for the entire season -- but their current +195 is slightly longer than the +170 they showed just one month ago. The Boston Red Sox and Atlanta Braves (both 14-1) round out the top six.

Meanwhile, the Chicago White Sox (close to locking down at least a wild-card spot) sit at 25-1. Chicago was an astonishing 400-1 before the season and is one of the largest liabilities in a variety of futures markets across the sportsbook marketplace.

Odds by DraftKings Sportsbook  at time of publication.

articles.headline: Lamine Camara better off in Monaco, ex-Chelsea midfielder says
articles.description: Chelsea transfer target Lamine Camara has been told he is better off where he is by Monaco teammate and former Blues cast-off Denis Zakaria.
articles.body:
Chelsea transfer target Lamine Camara has been told he is better off where he is by Monaco teammate and former Blues cast-off Denis Zakaria.

Zakaria spent a largely forgettable season on loan at Stamford Bridge from Juventus in 2022-23, making seven Premier League appearances under three different managers as the team finished 12th.

Camara was the subject of a last-minute bid from Chelsea on transfer deadline day before the Ligue 1 side pulled the plug for reasons the London club said were not explained.

The 22-year-old later said he had "turned the page" on the failed move to the Premier League, and he has been a central figure in Monaco's strong start to the season.

A 2-1 win at home against Lens kept Filipe Luis' side top of the table, after which Zakaria urged Camara to forget about the Blues.

"Chelsea? I told him that it was good but that it is better here," the Switzerland international told reporters after the game, according Get French Football News.

"I know the player and the person that he is. He is very professional. I think [the failed transfer] has given him even more strength. He was incredible [against Lens]."

A £47 million ($63 m) deal for the Senegal international was verbally agreed with Monaco in the final hours of the transfer window before the Ligue 1 side backed out at the last minute.

- Monaco's Lamine Camara says he has 'turned the page' after failed Chelsea move

- What's next for Camara, Sarr, Ait-Nouri and more after failed transfer window?

The U-turn left Chelsea furious, with one source telling the Press Association that Monaco's conduct had been "extraordinary and deeply unprofessional."

The team have looked light in midfield in the early weeks of the season following injury to Moisés Caicedo, who has played only 14 minutes so far, and the £125 m ($167 m) sale of Enzo Fernández to Manchester City on deadline day.

"There was a possibility I could leave," Camara told French media earlier in September. "It didn't go through at the last minute and that's part of football. I've turned the page and am focusing on the season."

Monaco lead the way in Ligue 1 by two points from Lyon and Paris FC -- who are coached by former Chelsea boss Liam Rosenior -- after winning four of their first five games of the season.

Manager Filipe Luis was a title winner as a player at Stamford Bridge in 2015 and was considered as a possible replacement for Rosenior before the club hired Xabi Alonso.

articles.headline: Ruben Amorim: 'I can't repeat my mistakes' after Man United
articles.description: Ruben Amorim has vowed not to repeat the mistakes of his Manchester United tenure at AC Milan.
articles.headlineJa: ルベン・アモリム：「マンUでの過ちを繰り返すわけにはいかない」
articles.descriptionJa: ルベン・アモリムは、マンチェスター・ユナイテッド在任中の過ちをACミランで繰り返さないことを誓った。
articles.body:
Ruben Amorim has vowed not to repeat the mistakes of his Manchester United tenure at AC Milan.

Amorim lost his job in Manchester after his trademark 3-4-3 formation failed to click. He was only in charge for 14 months, winning just 24 of his 63 matches.

Now in the dugout at Milan, he intends to learn from the past.

"I can't repeat my mistakes of Manchester United, if we don't have the characteristics to play in a certain style then we will adapt," Amorim was quoted by Gazzetta dello Sport.

His Milan side broke from his usual tactic by using a back four in a 3-0 win against Lecce in Italy's Serie A at the weekend. Christian Pulisic, Adrien Rabiot and Diego Moreira scored the goals.

Amorim added: "We'll go back to building with three, but we'll see. Here in Italy, the coaches are very good, especially at going after other teams one-on-one."

Luka Modric, 41, is still a mainstay in Milan's midfield.

- Man United's Michael Carrick concerned about Benjamin Sesko's latest injury

- Carrick quashes notion Manchester United are out of shape

- Michael Carrick keen to find Man United positives, but there aren't many right now

"With Modric, we need to have the ball for a long time, but he's ready to play every game we need," Amorim said. "If we only play transition games, it's not good for him."

Milan are fifth in Serie A after five games, two points behind leaders Roma.

His old side United, meanwhile -- now led permanently by Michael Carrick who initially replaced Amorim temporarily -- have started their Premier League campaign poorly with just one win in five.

articles.headline: Matheus Cunha urges calm after disproving 'Man United will go to Championship' fear
articles.description: Matheus Cunha has said it's too early to write off Manchester United this season after reminding critics they were able to recover from a poor start a year ago to finish third in the Premier League.
articles.headlineJa: マテウス・クーニャ、「マンUは降格する」との不安を打ち消し冷静さを呼びかける
articles.descriptionJa: マテウス・クーニャは、昨季不調なスタートから立て直してプレミアリーグ3位で終えたことを引き合いに出し、今季のマンチェスター・ユナイテッドを見限るのはまだ早すぎると語った。
articles.body:
Matheus Cunha has said it's too early to write off Manchester United this season after reminding critics they were able to recover from a poor start a year ago to finish third in the Premier League.

United won just two of their first seven games in all competitions under Ruben Amorim last season. The 1-1 draw at Fulham on Sunday means they've started the new campaign with the same record.

And Cunha, who scored the equaliser at Craven Cottage, insists the recovery under Carrick last season -- after Amorim had been dismissed in January -- shows that they can still be successful this term.

"Last season was my first season here, and then maybe it was more crazy than this one," Cunha said.

"There was a lot of noise around us, a season without Champions League. Maybe people were saying 'Oh, United will go to the Championship' or something like this.

"And then at the end of the day, we finished third, you know? I feel like inside of us, we still have a lot of trust, we know what we do, all the belief is inside."

United head into the extended three-week international break 12th in the table and without a win for three games.

- Why this 3-week international break is longest ever (and why that's a good thing)

- Cole Palmer withdraws from England's Nations League squad - sources

Cunha says the players are desperate to have the chance to put things right.

But the Brazilian accepted that with Carrick and his players under the spotlight because of their current form, maybe the lay-off has come at the right time.

United return to action in October with a tough run against Tottenham, Atletico Madrid and Como.

"I'm so anxious to play the next one," Cunha said.

"And then we have a big break now. Of course, when you don't win, you feel this kind of feeling to let's play the next one to win and feel everything good.

"But yeah, maybe it's the moment to be calm, to put the ideas in the right way, to come back. And then of course that could be a big month."

articles.headline: Miami Dolphins end road trip with more lessons than wins
articles.description: Miami's players, coaches say takeaways from 49ers blowout will be building blocks for the rest of the season.
articles.headlineJa: マイアミ・ドルフィンズ、アウェー遠征で勝利以上の教訓を得て終了
articles.descriptionJa: マイアミの選手やコーチ陣は、49ers戦の大敗から得た教訓が今季残りの試合の礎になると語っている。
articles.body:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- Just before the final two-minute warning of the Miami Dolphins' 35-13 loss to the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday, quarterback Malik Willis found receiver Ryan Miller for a 77-yard touchdown -- his first touchdown pass of the season and the team's longest passing touchdown since Week 1 of the 2024 season.

Willis wasn't impressed.

"I felt good for Ryan, I didn't feel good for the Miami Dolphins," he said. "That didn't help us. I mean, obviously it helped on the stat sheet, but it didn't help us as a team."

The Dolphins spent the past week in northern California in preparation for what offensive coordinator Bobby Slowik called "a really good challenge" against the 49ers, and will return home from this two-game road trip, after losing to the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 1, with more lessons than victories.

San Francisco scored touchdowns on each of its first five possessions, including both of their two offensive drives in the first half. Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley called the game "a tale of two halves" after Miami watched a 14-6 halftime deficit balloon to a 29-point hole within minutes.

Hafley said his team began the game strongly, but 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy found a wide-open George Kittle for a 40-yard completion on the first play of the second half, ultimately setting up a Kittle touchdown three plays later.

The 49ers went on to score two more touchdowns in their next 10 plays to put the game out of reach.

"We did something extremely uncharacteristic on the first play of the half that went for an explosive," Hafley said. "And we had another huge mistake that went for a touchdown. So quickly, it hit us in the face really hard in the second half. And we didn't coach well enough in the second half, we didn't play well enough. So really disappointing.

"Thought we had a great week of preparation and I felt like we were ready to play better. And the first half we did -- the second half was just not good enough in any phase."

The discrepancy in overall experience between the Dolphins and 49ers was clear in a game between the youngest and second-oldest teams in the NFL respectively. Seven of Miami's top 10 leaders in defensive snaps Sunday have played in the league for fewer than two seasons.

The veteran Purdy had more total touchdowns (3) than incompletions (2), and San Francisco's offense averaged 7.8 yards per play as 49ers receivers consistently found open field. According to NextGen Stats, Purdy's targets created 4.8 yards of separation on average, the most in the NFL this week.

"You've got guys who's [in] the second game ever in the league and they're playing a championship team," linebacker Jordyn Brooks said. "So it's like you don't want those things to happen, but I always look at things from the positive side and I'd rather them happen now, where we can learn from them and build later. As the season progresses, we get better and better.

articles.headline: The stat that could swing every NBA team's 2026-27 season
articles.description: Let's dive into the trends, storylines and statistical nuggets that could define the NBA season.
articles.headlineJa: NBA全チームの2026-27シーズンを左右する可能性のあるスタッツ
articles.descriptionJa: NBAのシーズンを決定づける可能性のあるトレンド、ストーリーライン、注目のスタッツ情報に迫る。
articles.body:
One of my favorite annual preseason traditions is to identify one number for every NBA team, sourced from a variety of data points and statistical categories, that highlights a key aspect of each squad entering the new season.

Last year, for instance, this exercise foreshadowed Jalen Johnson's breakout in Atlanta, the Milwaukee Bucks' struggles in Giannis Antetokounmpo's final season and the Portland Trail Blazers' league-worst turnover rate.

Let's dive into this year's 30 numbers to get a sense for the 2026-27 season to come, featuring all sorts of trends, storylines and statistical nuggets to monitor over the next 10 months.

Jump to a team:

ATL | BOS | BKN | CHA | CHI | CLE

DAL | DEN | DET | GS | HOU | IND

LAC | LAL | MEM | MIA | MIL | MIN

NO | NY | OKC | ORL | PHI | PHX

POR | SAC | SA | TOR | UTAH | WAS

Atlanta Hawks: 108.6

The Hawks allowed just 108.6 points per 100 possessions after the All-Star break, ranking second in the NBA in that span, behind only the Oklahoma City Thunder.

Over the whole season, the Hawks ranked 10th on defense -- and that was before they added Luguentz Dort, one of the most ferocious perimeter defenders in the NBA. Whether Dort and Dyson Daniels can survive on offense if and when they play together remains to be seen, but that duo with Nickeil Alexander-Walker plus Atlanta's other defensive infrastructure could combine to form one of the NBA's stingiest units.

Boston Celtics: 4

In all four of Joe Mazzulla's seasons as Boston's head coach, the Celtics have finished with a top-five offensive and defensive rating, per Cleaning the Glass. Only three other squads in that span have accomplished that feat: the 2023-24 Thunder, the 2024-25 Thunder and the 2025-26 San Antonio Spurs.

That consistent two-way excellence hasn't always translated to the playoffs. In those four seasons, Boston won one title but was upset in the three other series.

Yet after an offseason of turmoil, that consistency should also be encouraging for Celtics fans. Even without Jaylen Brown, their team will likely look like a championship contender on both sides once again -- in the regular season, at least.

Brooklyn Nets: 72%

Egor Demin was by far the best of the Nets' rookies last season, averaging 10.3 points per game and a solid assist-to-turnover ratio while making 38.5% of his 3-pointers. That latter statistic is especially encouraging for a player with shooting questions entering the NBA.

But Demin didn't find many ways to score other than 3-pointers, as 72% of his shot attempts last season were 3s. That was the 16th-highest rate out of 279 players with at least 1,000 minutes last season -- the three players immediately ahead of him were shooting specialists Klay Thompson, Gary Trent Jr. and Landry Shamet.
